diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Donald Trump spoke about the results of the Israeli parliamentary elections, saying he initially received "terrible" reports about Netanyahu's electoral prospects, but now the Israeli Prime Minister is "in a relatively good position." Trump added that he heard his support for Netanyahu had a significant impact. He said he has not yet thought about intervening to form a unity government but will consider it.

A released video shows the mother of the deceased Armin Teymouri-rad joining the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" by lighting a candle for her son. Armin Teymouri-rad, 19 years old, was killed on the evening of 19 Dey in Fardis.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said the country will stand in any situation and the current conditions can be an opportunity to increase resilience. He emphasized that the current threat is a compulsion and there is no choice. Pezeshkian added that spaces can be closed and preparations can be made for the current situation.

The Central Elections Committee of Israel announced that it has received the Likud party's request regarding allegations of widespread fraud by Arab parties and will review it within the framework of election integrity oversight. The committee emphasized that reviewing parties' requests about possible violations and the accuracy of election results is part of the usual oversight process. Also, Din Lione, the acting CEO of the committee, contacted parties about the process of reviewing possible election violations two days before the elections.

Niloufar Ardalan, head coach of Persepolis women's team, after the first women's football derby in Iran and a 2-1 victory over Esteghlal, said: "We achieved a historic win for Persepolis. It's a pity this match was not broadcast live. Even the club managers could not watch the game in person."

One day after the Israeli elections, it is still unclear which coalition will form the next government. Netanyahu's coalition has won 53 seats and Gadi Eizenkot's coalition has won 48 seats, and neither has reached the 61-seat threshold. Arab parties, having won 19 seats, could play a decisive role in forming the government.

Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, claimed on Wednesday, 6 Aban, that last year's Dey protests in Iran started from social networks. According to the Russian news agency Interfax, Putin said these networks were neither managed nor controlled by Iranian authorities, and the only action they could take was to cut everything off.

Na'im Qasim, Secretary-General of Hezbollah Lebanon, stated that they value the agreement between Iran and the US because it is, alongside resistance, the only source of power. He said the Islamic Republic prioritizes stopping Israeli attacks on Lebanon and the withdrawal of Israeli forces. Qasim also said the results of the Israeli elections are a sign of failure and it does not matter to them who leads Israel.
On Monday, 4 Aban, Ahmad Iranmanesh, a citizen from Saravan County, was arrested by security forces in this county and transferred to an unknown location.

The United Nations General Assembly is holding a meeting on the human rights crisis in Iran. In this meeting, Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights, and the independent international fact-finding committee will present their reports.

Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel issues, said the alignments are still unclear and the remaining votes need to be counted. He suggested the possibility of religious parties joining Netanyahu's rivals and said some Likud members might join the opposition to prevent a repeat election.

Persepolis women's football team defeated Esteghlal 2-1 in the first derby of the Iranian Women's Premier League and won this historic match. The match had various controversies; male spectators and journalists were banned from entering the stadium, and both clubs were not allowed to broadcast the match live.

Meir Javdanfar said Benjamin Netanyahu still has loyal support from a significant portion of voters despite widespread criticism. He predicted Netanyahu might use a new war against Iran to maintain power, but it is unlikely he will form the next government. Javdanfar considered the coalition of Gadi Eizenkot with Arab parties more likely and called it a historic achievement for Israel.

Reuters reported on Wednesday, 6 Aban that Qatari mediators presented a new draft agreement to Iran to end the war with the United States and Israel, but a senior Islamic Republic official said Doha only proposed "unacceptable" ideas and they cannot be considered an "offer." An informed official said the draft includes a seven-day timeline for confidence-building, and Iran's response is expected by the end of the week.

With over 85% of votes counted in the Israeli election, none of the factions have secured the necessary parliamentary majority to form a government. An interview with Arash Azizi, a history researcher and humanities lecturer at Yale University.

Jamshid Molaei, Esmail Molaei, Hossein Molaei, Armin Molaei, and Aref Dadvand, citizens of Izeh, have been held in judicial limbo in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz for over 70 days. Since their arrest, they have been deprived of phone contact and visits with their families. Jamshid, Esmail, and Hossein Molaei are relatives of Kian Pirfalak, a child killed during the nationwide protests of 1401.

Technical structure workers of Travers Company criticized the payment of only 75% of their October salaries. They say their salaries have been paid incompletely and with delay for several months and demand full payment of salaries and benefits every month.

United Students reported that Nabi Omidi, an associate professor of economics and financial management at Payame Noor University, has been sentenced to 9 years in prison, five years of which are enforceable, for his presence and support of the January 2027 protests in Malekshahi county. According to the report, he faced charges of "acting against national security," "propaganda against the system," and participation in protests. In addition to imprisonment, dismissal from the university, a travel ban, confiscation of his passport, and a ban on entering Malekshahi county have been announced as supplementary punishments for this university professor.
A citizen told Iran International in a video that each carton of electrodes has reached a price of 8,200,000 tomans, mentioning the rising prices and work stoppages in Iran.

A report states that the execution of a prisoner convicted of intentional murder in a group fight case was carried out in Kashan prison in Khordad. Also, three prisoners sentenced to death in Dargaz, Nishapur, and Dandi were released after the victims' families pardoned them. The General Directorate of Prisons in Isfahan province announced that 27 death penalty cases were settled in the first half of the current year.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that despite decades of propaganda and huge expenses to create hatred against Israel, the Islamic Republic has not achieved its goal. He also referred to the sympathy of Iranians with the people of Israel after the October 7 attack and their sensitivity to developments in that country.

Hadi Jamalipour, a political prisoner serving his sentence on furlough, was dismissed from his workplace. He was previously an employee at Payame Noor University in Birjand. A source close to his family confirmed that in Mehr month of this year, Jamalipour was dismissed by an order from the disciplinary council of Payame Noor University.
A released video shows the family of the late Arman Abed Moghami holding his birthday anniversary ceremony at his grave. Arman Abed Moghami, 35 years old, was killed in Rasht on 18 Dey 1404.

According to The Wall Street Journal, the US has warned Gulf countries to be prepared for the possibility of a short but intense military campaign in Iran after next week's midterm elections. Washington is also strengthening air defenses, supplying ammunition, and preparing fighter jets and bombers in the region.

Meir Javedanfar, an analyst on Israeli affairs, considered the winning of 27 seats by Likud as a sign of Netanyahu maintaining his voter base. He suggested Netanyahu might use a new war against Iran to retain power, but found it unlikely that Netanyahu would form the government and considered an Eisenkot coalition with Arab parties more probable.
Idris Mohammadzadeh, a citizen from Mahabad, was arrested on Saturday, 2 Aban, for the execution of a five-year and one-day prison sentence and was transferred to Mahabad prison.

Hossein Ahmadi, a detainee linked to the nationwide protests of Dey 1404, remains in legal limbo after 166 days of detention in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan. He suffers from physical problems in his back and neck and has been deprived of proper medical care and transfer to medical centers. This report was published by HRANA news agency.

Mohammad Reza Aref, the first deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian, criticized the lack of legal preparedness to address digital space issues and warned that continuing the current trend may lead to a crisis. He said that rulings are sometimes forcibly issued for the digital space based on the real space, which is unjustified. Aref ordered the formation of a permanent working group to gradually review and draft laws related to the digital space.

Yair Golan, leader of the Israeli Democratic Party, announced he will meet with three leaders of parties opposing Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday, 7 Aban, but did not disclose their names. These meetings occur as neither of the two main blocs in the Israeli parliamentary elections secured the 61 seats needed to form a government. Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, previously urged parties to negotiate to avoid a new election.

The Communications Office of the Turkish Presidency announced that Recep Tayyip Erdoğan spoke with Donald Trump about bilateral relations, developments in the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen, and the Ukraine war. Erdoğan said that as the Makkah Joint Defense Coalition, they closely monitor developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen and strive to resolve these issues diplomatically.
With 86% of Israeli votes counted, Netanyahu's coalition leads with 53 seats. Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal revealed that the US has warned Gulf countries of an imminent intense war with Iran.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, stated that in one case, 34 people were tried over five days, 12 were sentenced to death, and seven have been executed so far. She said at least 34 people have been executed in connection with the protests of Dey 1401, and at least five were executed publicly. Thousands have been arrested on security charges, and families of the victims face pressure to remain silent.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) on Wednesday, 6 Aban, denied reports by media controlled by the Islamic Republic about commercial ships hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM stated that US forces have cleared all main maritime routes in this waterway of mines and these routes remain mine-free. CENTCOM emphasized that these claims are false and thousands of commercial ships have safely passed through these routes so far.
A video received shows that the fourth anniversary ceremony of Ali Fazeli and Hadi Chaksari, protesters killed in the Mahsa uprising, was held at their graves.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke by phone with Donald Trump about bilateral relations and regional and global issues. Erdogan emphasized efforts to strengthen cooperation on the occasion of the 100th anniversary of relations between the two countries. He also said Turkey is working within a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to resolve issues related to the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen and is ready to support efforts to revive diplomatic talks between Ukraine and Russia.

According to Oscar Puente, Spain's Minister of Transport, a Renfe train was allowed to continue moving despite a red signal caused by a computer communication failure, due to a wrong decision. In the collision of this train with another in Orda, 68 people were killed and dozens injured. This is the second deadly rail accident in Spain this year.

Axios reported, citing three American, Israeli, and regional sources, that Qatar, with the support of several regional countries, is trying to reach an agreement between Washington and Tehran to resume negotiations and prevent the outbreak of war after the US midterm elections. Qatar is trying to convince the Islamic Republic to allow International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors to visit the bombed nuclear facilities in Iran in exchange for reducing some US sanctions. Axios wrote that if diplomatic efforts fail, there is a possibility of a new round of US and Israeli attacks shortly after the midterm elections.

Milan and Inter clubs are scheduled to unveil the design of their new stadium in Milan tomorrow night. This project, which is expected to be completed by 2031, will have a capacity of 71,500 people, making it one of the five largest stadiums in Europe. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the design of the new stadium has been entrusted to 91-year-old architect Norman Foster and the Manica architecture firm.

The Dutch representative at the Third Committee meeting of the UN General Assembly called for the immediate halt of illegal executions, arbitrary detentions, and violence against the people of Iran. He referred to reports confirming widespread human rights violations by the Islamic Republic, including a significant increase in deadly force and mass arrests of protesters. He also expressed regret over the killing of civilians, including children, and called for a diplomatic solution to the war and full respect for international law by all parties, urging international support for holding perpetrators accountable.

The UK representative at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee stated that women and girls in Iran continue to face discrimination, arrest, and prosecution for not complying with mandatory hijab laws. He referred to reports of at least 34 protesters executed since Dey 1404 and called for an immediate halt to the executions. He also condemned the torture of detainees, widespread internet shutdowns, and the repression of ethnic and religious minorities in Iran.

The European Union representative announced that since Dey 1404, the EU has sanctioned 37 individuals and 9 entities for their role in human rights violations in Iran and is ready to take further actions if necessary. He said at the Third Committee meeting of the UN General Assembly that the Islamic Republic's security forces responded to protesters' demands with excessive violence and internal repression has increased. The EU representative called for an immediate halt to executions, release of arbitrary detainees, and an end to discrimination against women.

The Swiss representative at the Third Committee meeting of the UN General Assembly stated that some human rights violations in Iran since September 2025, according to the independent international fact-finding mission, constitute crimes against humanity. He condemned the use of the death penalty, called for a halt to executions, conversion of death sentences to other punishments, and support for human rights defenders. He also emphasized that Iranian authorities must respect due process and provide unhindered access to UN bodies.

Israel's representative at the UN General Assembly Third Committee called for a comprehensive review of killings, executions, and arbitrary detentions in Iran. He described the Islamic Republic as a destabilizing force in the Middle East and a supporter of groups like Hamas and Hezbollah. He also referred to protests in Iran, urging UN attention and action.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the United States has informed several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short but intense military campaign after the US midterm elections. The US military is transferring a Patriot missile defense system from Texas to strengthen its missile defense capabilities and has withdrawn forces from bases near Iran. US forces in the region are replenishing ammunition supplies and fighter jets are preparing for attacks.

The widow of the late Shahrouz Mehrabi joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" and lit a candle for him, saying, "From every drop of your blood, a sprout will grow." Shahrouz Mehrabi, 36 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Saveh.

Two days after the Ballon d'Or ceremony, France Football introduced a new award called "BOAT" to select the best Ballon d'Or in history. The winner of this award is Cristiano Ronaldo, specifically for his 2008 Ballon d'Or. The voting for this award was done by the magazine's users, with each vote costing one euro.

A video shows the father of Fereydoun Mahmoudi, a protester killed in the Mahsa uprising, reciting poetry with mothers seeking justice at his son's grave. This 32-year-old protester was killed on 28 Shahrivar 1401 in Saqqez.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said reports from inside Iran show that the Israeli election has become the main topic of conversation among people in society. He added that many people hope Netanyahu will be elected and that the number of Netanyahu supporters in Iran's 90 million population is much higher than his supporters in Israel's 10 million population.
The Persepolis women's football team players celebrated with their fans at Ghal'eh Hasan Khan Stadium after winning 2-1 against Esteghlal in the first women's derby.

Donald Trump responded to a Wall Street Journal report about JD Vance sending a letter to Mohsen Rezaei to resume peace talks with Iran. Trump said he did not order Vance to negotiate and that the main goal is to help Iran with medical supplies. The report also states that Vance is assessing the possibility of finding common ground to prevent an attack on Iran.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said this Israeli election cycle is very important for Iranians because the overthrow of the Islamic Republic is the main priority for the Iranian people, and they believe Netanyahu is the most determined person in overthrowing the Islamic Republic.

Mansheh Amir said Gadi Eisenkot, despite efforts to form a coalition, faces serious obstacles due to disagreements among parties opposing Netanyahu and winning fewer seats than expected. He added that Eisenkot's coalition with Arab parties will also be difficult due to political differences. Amir predicted that if government formation talks fail and new elections are held, Netanyahu's position may strengthen.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said the Israeli elections are directly related to the overthrow of the Islamic Republic. He added that killing Khamenei and many IRGC commanders who ordered repression and massacres has made Netanyahu popular among the majority of the Iranian people.

Jamshid Barzegar said Qatar's new proposal, supported by several regional countries, includes Iran's return to cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency, resumption of nuclear inspections, and limited oil sales and partial release of Iran's frozen assets. He added that Tehran's opposition to these proposals has increased the likelihood of renewed attacks by the US and Israel. Barzegar said the Islamic Republic's policies in the Strait of Hormuz have had the opposite effect and placed the regime in a strategic deadlock.

Ali Sadrazadeh said that if the negotiations between the Islamic Republic and the United States fail and a new war begins, Israel's political equations will change. He added that such a war could sideline party disputes over government formation and pave the way for a national coalition including Netanyahu and Eisenkot. Sadrazadeh emphasized that the fate of the Tehran-Washington talks could play a role in determining the composition of Israel's future government.

Following reports by American media about the possibility of new military attacks against Iran, questions have arisen about how the occurrence of war might strengthen Benjamin Netanyahu's position in negotiations to form Israel's future government. Netanyahu may remain as interim prime minister or be tasked with forming a new government, and his role in deciding to start military operations and the political and legal consequences of such action are under discussion. Conversations with Ben Sabti and David Matai have been conducted on this topic.

Local officials in Taiz province, Yemen, have called for an immediate investigation into reports that Houthi forces may have used artillery shells containing toxic and banned substances. This request came after reports from the Al-Qurouq and Kahlan fronts. They called for the involvement of the United Nations and international organizations in the investigations.

Ashkan Nezamabadi, an economic journalist, said Iran's economy is facing stagflation with negative growth and inflation close to 90 percent. He added that Masoud Pezeshkian's government lacks the authority to make decisions on major economic issues and controlling inflation is not possible without changes in macro policies. Nezamabadi also attributed the retreat from implementing the fourth gasoline price to concerns about social and security consequences and said the government has opted for gradual quota reductions instead of a sudden price increase.

According to Mexican media, Mexican TV host Ernesto Chavana kicked a drone on October 26 during the live show “S Show” in Monterrey, and the drone hit the face of model Isabella Rojas. Media reported that Rojas's lip was cut, and Chavana apologized live on air, taking responsibility. The show's production team confirmed that he would cover the costs resulting from the injury.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said that the Islamic Republic faces problems producing drones due to electricity shortages. He added that the US destroyed Iran's nuclear enrichment capacity through military operations and called the Islamic Republic the biggest supporter of terrorism. Trump also emphasized that Iran must never have nuclear weapons.

The UK government announced on Wednesday, 6 Aban, that to reduce the pressure of rising energy prices due to the Iran war, it will pay £100 financial aid to 20 million eligible households and extend the reduction of electricity VAT until July 2027. John Healey, the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, said the war in the Middle East and rising energy costs have put significant pressure on household budgets and the country's economy. According to the announced plan, households in tax groups A to D in England will receive £100 from January 2027.

A court in Syria sentenced Abduljabbar Ghazi Arziq, a member of the paramilitary group Liwa al-Quds affiliated with the IRGC, to life imprisonment on charges of membership in an armed group linked to war crimes and crimes against humanity. The court stated that this group operated to provoke civil war and escalate sectarian conflicts. The director of the Accountability and Judicial Follow-up Department at the Syrian National Commission for Transitional Justice said the severity of the crimes and their threat to civilians were factors in issuing the sentence.

Kambiz Tavana, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Washington intends to intensify economic pressure and maritime blockade against the Islamic Republic. According to him, Bassett emphasized that the US tariff and economic campaign will become more intense in the next eight weeks. Washington expects Tehran to take practical action first if it returns to diplomacy.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, stated that the Islamic Republic has used wartime conditions to intensify repression, increase arrests, and carry out executions. The European Union representative at the Third Committee of the UN General Assembly strongly condemned the rise in executions following the nationwide protests in Dey month. Nazli Sedghi explained the obstacles to more serious international responses to the Islamic Republic beyond condemning widespread human rights violations in Iran.

The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported that since the beginning of August, more than 281,000 people have been displaced due to intensified clashes between Yemeni government forces and Houthis. The agency warned that three-quarters of the displaced face shortages of shelter, clean water, and health services, and over 230,000 people need emergency assistance. The UN Population Fund warned about increased risks of sexual violence, human trafficking, and forced marriage, especially in crowded displacement sites.

Kamyar Behrang, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that the Islamic Republic's insistence on maintaining its enrichment program, despite claims of not wanting nuclear weapons, has increased concerns about Tehran potentially moving towards building such weapons. He said that a possible withdrawal of the Islamic Republic from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty could add to these concerns. Behrang emphasized that from the Trump administration's perspective, the main issue is no longer just limiting the level of enrichment but preventing the continued operation of centrifuges.

Amir Hamidi said the seven-day negotiations are not merely a diplomatic effort to prevent war but part of Washington's pressure strategy on the Islamic Republic. He added that the US, while maintaining military readiness, demands Tehran accept specific and verifiable commitments on its nuclear program, missile activities, Strait of Hormuz security, and regional policies. Hamidi emphasized that the end of this deadline does not necessarily mean the start of a military attack, and Washington's decision depends on intelligence assessments and potential consequences.

At least 68 people have died and dozens have been injured following a collision between two high-speed trains in Spain. Rescue operations are ongoing and the exact cause of the accident is still unknown.

Kor Pour, an Iranian-British painter, linked Iranian carpet patterns with East Asian art at the "Entry Points" exhibition in Tokyo. He addresses themes such as migration and cultural journeys, inspired by childhood memories and living between different cultures.

Asia-Pacific media reported that Israel's political deadlock after the parliamentary elections indicates difficulties in forming a new government. Singapore and Taiwan media also reported that a change of government in Israel will not necessarily lead to a change in the country's strategy towards the Islamic Republic, and Donald Trump's future decisions will play a decisive role in military confrontation.

Two days after the Israeli parliamentary elections on the 5th of Aban, counting over 91% of votes shows Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition leading with 53 seats. The counting of "double envelope" votes, including absentee voters such as soldiers and prisoners, has also begun. The Likud party holds the most seats among parties with 26 seats.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the US has warned Gulf Arab countries about the possibility of a short but intense operation against the Islamic Republic. The newspaper wrote that there are new signs of readiness of the US and Israeli militaries for a possible wave of attacks aimed at forcing Tehran to negotiate.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, reported that at least 34 people have been executed in connection with nationwide protests in Iran. She criticized the arrests, brief trials, and forced confessions, calling for a halt to executions, the release of prisoners, and guarantees of fair trials.

Vincent Kompany, the Belgian coach of Bayern Munich who was hospitalized due to meningitis, was discharged after five days to recover at home. Max Eberl, the sports director of Bayern Munich, announced that Kompany's hospitalization was caused by meningitis. The 40-year-old coach, who had suffered a viral infection about ten days earlier, has now returned home with medical permission.

Hassan Yazdani lost 7-5 to Arash Yoshida in the round of 16 of the 97 kg freestyle wrestling World Championship. Yazdani was leading 5-2 in the second period but Yoshida changed the result in the final seconds. Yazdani must now wait for Yoshida to reach the final to enter the repechage group.

With over 90% of the votes counted in the Israeli election, Benjamin Netanyahu's party and its allies have won 53 seats, and the opposition party has won 48 seats. Neither of the two blocs in the Knesset, Israel's 120-seat parliament, has reached the majority needed to form a government.
A video shows the wife of the unnamed protester Parsa Loinian holding a memorial ceremony and lighting a candle for him. This 31-year-old protester was killed on 19 Dey 1404 in Isfahan.

Leila Morvati, a political analyst, says Turkey and Pakistan are trying to reduce tensions between Tehran and Washington due to their proximity to Iran and concerns about the consequences of war. She added that Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and other Arab countries in the region are also seeking mediation. However, the unresolved dispute over the Islamic Republic's nuclear program remains a major obstacle to reaching an agreement or a lasting ceasefire.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the Iraqi Prime Minister's trip to Syria is a sign of a new alignment forming in the region; an alignment in which Baghdad and Damascus seek to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz and curb the influence of the Islamic Republic and its proxy groups.

Jalil Moghaddam, deputy coordinator of the Islamic Republic Navy, announced that this force has named an area 500 to 600 kilometers from the Strait of Hormuz as "Tangeh Ohad Velayat" and has drawn a line for it. Moghaddam said that vessels "do not dare to pass through this area."
A video sent to Iran International shows a protester writing the slogan "Until the cleric is shrouded, this homeland will not be a homeland" on the wall of a public passage.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that the exchange of letters between JD Vance and Mohsen Rezaee is a normal part of diplomacy but is unlikely to lead to constructive negotiations. He added that the political deadlock in Israel and the approaching US midterm elections may not diminish the military option. It is also possible that Netanyahu uses this situation to persuade the Trump administration to take military action against the Islamic Republic.

Stephen Curry, the 38-year-old Golden State superstar, scored 44 points in a 119-114 victory over Minnesota, marking his fifteenth 40-point game after age 35 and matching LeBron James' historic record. Curry had an exceptional performance in this game, and Golden State's coach said Curry can always change the course of the game. Despite Golden State's 24-point lead at one point, Minnesota did not give up, and Curry had to play close to the 32-minute limit set for his time on the court.

Rahman Amouzad, Iran's 65 kg freestyle wrestling representative, lost 3-2 to Vazgen Tovanyan from Armenia in the quarterfinals of the World Championships and failed to advance to the semifinals. Amouzad, like Hassan Yazdani, lost the match in the final seconds. He must wait for Tovanyan to reach the final to return to the competition through the repechage group and compete for a bronze medal.

Messages and reports received by Iran International indicate an increase in food prices, including bread, chicken, meat, and tea. Citizens say the rising food prices have made it difficult for many people to meet their daily needs.

With over 91% of the votes counted in the Israeli parliamentary elections, neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eizenkot has achieved the majority needed to form a government. Four scenarios facing Israel include forming a national unity government, an opposition coalition supported by Arab parties, right-wing parties joining Netanyahu's coalition, or holding early elections. Reza Mohaddes, a reporter for Iran International, examines these scenarios and the obstacles facing each.

Nabi Omidi, a dismissed associate professor of economics and financial management at Payame Noor University, was sentenced to 9 years in prison by the Ilam Province Court of Appeal. This sentence had previously been issued by the Ilam Revolutionary Court and was confirmed as is in the appeal stage. He was convicted on charges including acting against national security, propaganda against the regime, and participating in protests, with 5 years of the sentence enforceable under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code.

Hebrew media reported that Shin Bet, Israel's internal security agency, is investigating the possibility of money transfers from abroad, including Qatar and Turkey, to organizations encouraging electoral participation in the Arab community in Israel. This investigation began after the head of the Central Elections Committee requested a probe into Likud party allegations of foreign funding and possible electoral bribery.

The European Union representative at the Third Committee of the UN General Assembly announced that since December 1404, the EU has sanctioned 37 individuals and 9 entities for human rights violations in Iran. The representative expressed concern over the suppression of the December 1404 protests, use of deadly force, increased arbitrary arrests, torture, and executions. They also called for an end to executions, release of arbitrarily detained individuals, and accountability for human rights violators.

Omid Faraghat, a journalist imprisoned in the Central Prison of Karaj, was sentenced by the second branch of the Revolutionary Court of this city to 10 years and one day in prison, permanent dismissal from government and public services, and two years of prohibition from journalistic activity.

Hassan Yazdani, captain of Iran's freestyle wrestling team, was defeated by Arash Yoshida, an Iranian-Japanese wrestler, in the round of 16 at the World Championships. Rahman Amouzad also failed to reach the semifinals after losing to an opponent from Armenia. An interview was conducted with sports reporter Mehdi Rostampour.

The online media "Azad" announced the lifting of restrictions and resumption of its activities after about two months of suspension by judicial order. This media had previously been banned from publishing new programs following a criminal complaint by the Tehran prosecutor's office.

The Spanish Football Federation fined Barcelona 602 euros after Atletico Madrid complained about negotiations to sign Julian Alvarez. The disciplinary committee considered the act a minor violation and imposed the maximum fine. Barcelona denied any wrongdoing and plans to appeal.

Amir Mohammad Najafi was killed on 18 Dey in Fardis Karaj by gunfire from the suppressive forces of the Islamic Republic. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in Canada gathered on Wednesday, 6 Aban, in front of the CBC media office in Halifax and demanded media coverage of the crimes of the Islamic Republic.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the simultaneous emphasis by Donald Trump on "finishing the work of the Islamic Republic" and the sending of a letter from JD Vance to Mohsen Rezaei indicates that communication channels between Washington and Tehran remain open. According to Kazemian, this letter could be the last diplomatic effort by the US to reach an agreement, but disagreements over the Islamic Republic's nuclear program, the Strait of Hormuz, and support for proxy forces have clouded the prospects for an agreement and increased the risk of war.

Student and youth organizations in France continue to plan protests. Restrictions on gatherings and possible curfews have intensified the debate about the right to protest in the country. In Germany, after the announcement of far-left groups joining the demonstrations, police officials have warned about the possibility of violent actions.

The New York Times reported that direct negotiations between Tehran and Washington may begin next week in Qatar or Turkey. If Tehran accepts JD Vance's proposal letter, negotiations will technically start without preconditions, but Iran's nuclear program must be on the table. The report also mentioned diplomatic efforts by regional countries to reduce tensions and concerns about the risk of war.

Amin Ghanbari, a journalist from Semnan and manager of the Telegram channel "Payamgou-ye Semnan," has been sentenced to 20 years in prison by the first branch of the Revolutionary Court of that city. The charges against Ghanbari include "media action against the Islamic Republic," "assembly and collusion," "propaganda activity against the regime," "support for Pahlavi and the victims of Dey 1404 protests," and "insulting the founder of the Islamic Republic." Ghanbari was arrested in front of his house in Ordibehesht this year, and no details about the case, evidence, or his place of detention have been released.

A judge in Italy ordered the release of Youssef Sihr, a journalist and activist accused of inciting violence in Milan protests. Sihr, whom police identified as the administrator of the "October 17 Movement" Telegram group, was arrested on October 24 on charges of incitement to commit crimes with terrorist aims. Giorgia Meloni, Italy's Prime Minister, called his release "shameful" and humiliating for the police and investigators.

Israel held five parliamentary elections in less than four years from 2019 to 2022; a period marked by deadlock in forming a government, the formation and collapse of coalitions, and the return of Benjamin Netanyahu to power. Now, if parties do not reach an agreement to form a government, there is a possibility of holding elections again.
A video published on social media shows a group of customers of Saipa automotive company gathering due to delays in the delivery of Shahin Plus and regular Shahin cars.

IRNA reported on the occupational and livelihood challenges of environmental guards. Shortage of personnel, salaries not matching living costs, and uncertainty about employment status are among their main problems. The commander of the Environmental Protection Unit emphasized the need to provide equipment and improve the working conditions of environmental guards.

Houshang Seydali, the coordination manager of the National Iranian Gas Company, announced that gas supply conditions for the upcoming winter have become more difficult and planning has been done to provide alternative fuels such as gas cylinders and kerosene. He said about 11 provinces may face gas shortages, with three northern provinces having more difficult conditions. Seydali considered electricity the best option for home energy supply, provided sufficient electricity can be produced.
The public and revolutionary prosecutor of South Khorasan announced the closure of three cafes in Birjand due to violations related to religious regulations and public decency.

A group of Spanish citizens clashed with police in Madrid on Wednesday, 6 Aban, protesting against the government after a deadly train collision. About 500 people gathered in front of the Ministry of Transport and threw bottles and incendiary materials at the police. Officers used tear gas to disperse the protesters.

The Intelligence Department of Sistan and Baluchestan Province reported the arrest of 19 people in the central and southern counties of the province. According to this security agency, some of the detainees had connections with the US and Israel and were involved in the killing of several law enforcement officers in Iranshahr county. Three others are accused of collecting and sending information about defense and security centers.

Stopping or delays in the passage of more than four thousand trucks at the Iran-Turkey borders and the increase in maritime transport costs have raised concerns about the transfer of goods and the supply of essential needs of the people. The head of the Transport Commission of the Tehran Chamber of Commerce said the cost of transporting a 40-foot container from China has risen from about $2,700 to $2,800 to $13,600. Reports of similar problems on the routes of Iraq and Pakistan have also been raised.

Viviana Krsticic, a member of the UN fact-finding mission on Iran, stated that based on the mission's findings, many human rights violations by officials and institutions of the Islamic Republic in Iran during 2026 constitute crimes against humanity. She mentioned arbitrary arrests, torture, sexual violence, denial of fair trial, and arbitrary deprivation of the right to life. Switzerland condemns the use of the death penalty and emphasizes support for halting executions and protecting human rights defenders.

The death sentence of Leila Abolhasani, a 43-year-old citizen and detainee from the December 1404 protests, was overturned by the Supreme Court and her case was returned to the court for retrial. She had previously been sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court on charges of "moharebeh" (waging war against God). This sentence overturn followed an appeal by her lawyer.
On Thursday, 7 Aban around 16:00, it was reported that a large fire occurred on the Tehran-Karaj highway. Received images from citizens show this incident.

On the occasion of the 7th of Aban, the day commemorating Cyrus, a citizen told Iran International that this day is a reminder of a civilization's glory rooted deep in the history of this land and a day of a man whose name is intertwined with the greatness of Iran.

Moloud Hajizadeh, an economic journalist, said some households had previously replaced rice with bread, but now they have no substitute for bread either. He added that continuing this trend could turn bread supply for lower income groups into a crisis and expand livelihood protests.

A video received by Iran International on Thursday, 7 Aban, shows a large fire in a building at kilometer 11 of Karaj Special Road. It is said that the burning building belongs to Tehran Darou Company.

The Islamic Republic has again this year, as in the past decade, banned people's presence at the historical site of Pasargadae on Cyrus Day and restricted the routes leading to Cyrus's tomb. Despite these restrictions, Iran International's audience said that the name Cyrus has become a point of identity and a symbol for recalling the right to freedom and human dignity.

Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced three detainees of the December 1404 protests to death. Amir Reza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahramani, and a cleric named Mehdi were sentenced on charges of operational action for Israel. Mehdi was also sentenced to death in a separate case by the Special Clerical Court for apostasy.

Reports include paying 500,000 tomans subsidy for buying bread and pickles compared to house prices in 1979 in Kermanshah. Employees of Atlas Air have not received several months of salaries, and prices of motor oil and the drug Fluphenazine have sharply increased. Some bakeries are accused of methods to sell government-subsidized flour on the free market.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, announced that the country is making every effort to reduce tensions and help fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz amid the consequences of the Iran war. He said he spoke with Donald Trump last week about the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Burnham emphasized that this process must occur without any nuclear capabilities in Iran.

Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesperson, announced that Russia is ready to mediate between the Islamic Republic and the United States if requested. He said the issue of Iran is always raised in Moscow-Washington contacts and Russia wants to prevent military conflict in the Persian Gulf. Peskov also stated that if the dispute is over Iran's enriched uranium, Moscow is ready to transfer it to Russian territory.

Informed sources told Iran International that 10 plainclothes agents raided the homes of Raouf Rouhani Najafabadi, his mother Ferdows Ferdousian, and his mother-in-law Forough Darab in Isfahan on November 5, confiscating a large number of their belongings over six hours. According to these sources, the masked agents confiscated 9 mobile phones, 3 televisions, 3 laptops, a home theater system, several cameras, 4 musical instruments, over 15 suitcases and bags, over 30 million tomans in cash, all gold and jewelry, and some other items. A few days before this raid, Raouf Rouhani Najafabadi's wife had received an SMS from Article 49 Court, which is related to property confiscation and the "Headquarters for Executing Imam Khomeini's Order."

Tasnim reported that the trip of Tractor Tabriz football team to Oman for the match against Neftchi Uzbekistan in the Asian Elite League has become uncertain due to the flight permit not being issued. The team is scheduled to host Neftchi in Oman on Monday, 11 Aban in the fourth week of the Asian Elite League, but the flight permit has not yet been issued. Javad Nekounam warned that if another long trip is forced, the youth team will participate instead of the main team.

Branch 23 of Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced Amir Reza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, and Mehdi, a cleric whose last name was not announced, three detainees of the January 2026 protests, to death. Harana reported that this sentence was communicated to the three prisoners in prison on Monday, October 26. The charges against them include "operational action for Israel."
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing disturbances to people and traffic caused by government protesters.

A citizen reported that on the day of commemorating Cyrus, they were inspected more than 10 times on the route from Yazd to Shiraz and were not allowed to enter Pasargadae. He said Cyrus's value lies in his intellectual and human legacy, not just in conquests. He also referred to the importance of Cyrus Day as a symbol of management combined with humanity and a reminder of concepts such as tolerance and human rights.

Israel's Likud party called for police and Shin Bet involvement in the election manipulation case and announced it will present hundreds of testimonies and evidence for review. The party claimed foreign entities intervened in the elections by bribing voters to change the balance of power in the Knesset and remove the right-wing government. Meanwhile, Israeli police announced the arrest of seven more people suspected of election bribery in favor of the Arab party Ra'am.

The United Nations reported in its latest report that opium production in Afghanistan has increased fivefold. The report states that opium production in 2026 has reached nearly 1500 tons, about five times that of the previous year.

Heavy rains and flooding in various parts of Syria have killed at least two people and forced hundreds of families to leave their homes. Syrian officials reported that seven bridges and communication routes have become inaccessible, and the flood has damaged homes and refugee camps. Warnings about continued rainfall and the possibility of flooding remain in place.

A report states that three citizens from Baneh, including two 17-year-old teenagers named Ilya Lotfi Tormakchi and Zhiyar Rasouli, and an 18-year-old named Mohammad Faraji, remain in indefinite detention in a security detention center in Sanandaj despite 10 days having passed since their arrest.

According to information received by Iran International, the mothers of Ali Alavi and Saeed Najafi, who are among the martyrs of the Dey protests, died less than 10 months after their sons were killed. Ali Alavi, 35 years old, was killed on 19 Dey in Fardis, Karaj, and Saeed Najafi, 34 years old, was killed on 18 Dey in Naziabad, Tehran by suppression forces. More details in an interview with Farnoush Faraji, a member of the Iran International editorial team.

Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, CEO of Qatar Energy, said he met twice in the past two weeks with the acting Iranian Oil Minister and both sides are exploring oil and gas cooperation after the war ends. Al-Kaabi said Qatar Energy is buying long-term liquefied natural gas from the US and other suppliers to offset losses from the Iran war and protect its revenues against possible disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. He added these purchases are part of Qatar Energy's strategy to hedge commercial risks and exploit price differences in the global gas market.

Kyriakos Mitsotakis, Prime Minister of Greece, on Thursday, 7 Aban, called for a global ceasefire in maritime transport and stated that attacks on civilian commercial ships are unacceptable and threaten international trade and security. He said at a UN Security Council meeting that commercial ships should be able to navigate freely and safely even during military conflicts. Mitsotakis added that disruption of shipping freedom increases costs and instability in global markets.

Ali Sadrozadeh, a Middle East analyst, considered Netanyahu's coalition with opposition parties difficult and said that the occurrence of a war with the Islamic Republic could change the calculations of government formation.
